_comment: Targets for scripts/icon-ink.mjs. Every number here is the INTENDED ink size, in CSS
pixels, on the glyph's long axis. It is a decision, not a measurement: the measurement
is what the script prints, and the gap between the two is the bug.
defaultWant applies to any glyph without its own entry. Give a glyph its own entry only
when it genuinely should read a different size from its neighbours, and say why.

_note: A plus and a minus are bare strokes reaching the extremes of their box with nothing
in between, so the eye reads their full extent as the glyph. A gear at the same
MEASURED size is a dense shape whose bulk sits inboard of its widest teeth. Matched by
the ruler, the cross reads a size larger than everything around it. This is the one
place in this repo where a number is an optical judgement rather than a measurement,
which is exactly why it lives in this file, out loud, instead of being quietly baked
into SIZE_FACTOR where it would look like a result.
